items.item: CI-4 one attempt and finite window (freezable guards for event, run_attempt == 1 and ref/workflow_ref == refs/heads/main; single-queue concurrency without cancel; named dispatcher; runner-start admission against the window; Samuel's choice of not-after vs removal commit; consumption rule including pre-test refusals and no-step failures; honest split between machine and procedural restrictions)
items.evidence: Guards: md:59 gives workflow_dispatch, refs/heads/main and path@refs/heads/main; md:60 gives run_attempt == 1 and adds run_number == 1. json:1984-1988 and json:2005 match. Concurrency: md:62 gives one fixed group, cancel-in-progress false, at most one active and one pending run, described as 'Serialization only; not one-total-attempt enforcement or a promise that all queued requests survive'. This matches the GitHub doc (default queue single; a pending run is cancelled). json:1990-1991 and json:2004 agree. Dispatcher: md:55 proposes Samuel, with the actor login and ID to be recorded and nothing inferred; md:61; json:1993 is null and json:2008-2011 holds the recommendation. Admission: md:64 checks at job start before checkout, pull, install or test, refuses outside the window or with less than 1800 s remaining, and excludes queue time. json:1992 is JOB_START_ON_RUNNER. Window choice: json:1995-1999 has windowMechanismChoice null and lists NOT_AFTER_FROZEN_IN_BYTES and NAMED_OWNED_TRIGGER_REMOVAL_COMMIT; json:2012 recommends not-after; md:55 says every item is 'RECOMMENDED / OWNER DECISION PENDING'; md:63 has notBefore and notAfter null. Consumption: md:69 is labelled 'Proposed'. The attempt is consumed 'as soon as GitHub accepts the event and creates its run, including queued/cancelled runs, guard/admission/resource refusals, checkout/setup failure and every pre-test refusal'. Unknown delivery is held unavailable until reconciled. md:71 says 'Cancellation, failure, timeout' consume the attempt and need new authority. No-step GitHub-side failures are covered because the rule triggers on run creation, though they are not named. json:2000 and json:2287 are null. Honest split: md:67 says 'run_attempt alone cannot reject a second fresh dispatch'; md:69 says 'Guards cannot prevent a user from submitting an extra event'; md:71 says 'Current machine enforcement is NOT ESTABLISHED. Concurrency and user procedure are explicitly separate'; json:2023-2029 lists the procedural restrictions. Nonblocking defects: M-1 (run_number guard against option (b)), M-2 (self-referential 'exact frozen workflow SHA' guard), M-3 (cross-ref caveat missing), M-4 (step order for frozen window and actor values).

defects.title: Run-number guard cannot be satisfied under the still-listed option (b)
defects.claim: Revision 2 calls the run_number == 1 guard 'essential' (md:67) and makes it the only machine control against a second fresh dispatch. It holds only for a new workflow file with verified empty history. Option (b) adds a guarded pilot job to checks.yml, and that is still listed as a live owner choice (json:330-336, structureChoice null at json:323). checks.yml already has at least five runs, and its run_number grows with every PR and main-push run, so under (b) the guard always refuses. The alternative is dropping the guard, which removes the fresh-dispatch control. Revision 2 does not say this.
defects.evidence: md:60 says 'github.run_number == 1 ... for a newly created, verified unused workflow identity'. json:2005-2006 has requiredRunNumber 1 and newUnusedWorkflowIdentityAndHistoryProofRequired. CI_ROUTE_EXISTING_RUN_EVIDENCE_20261009.json@e01f8ea:13-70 shows five checks.yml pull_request runs (attempts 2, 1, 1, 1, 1). The GitHub contexts doc says run_number is 'A unique number for each run of a particular workflow in a repository.'
defects.fix: In CI-1 and CI-4, state that the run_number guard assumes option (a). If Samuel chooses (b), a different fresh-attempt mechanism must be specified and reviewed before the freeze. Alternatively, mark (b) as incompatible with the recommended attempt contract.

defects.title: 'Exact frozen workflow SHA' is listed as a machine guard that frozen bytes cannot contain
defects.claim: md:59 lists 'exact frozen workflow SHA' under 'Machine guard required in future frozen bytes'. github.workflow_sha is the commit SHA of the workflow file. A file cannot contain the SHA of the commit that contains it, and under the recommended PR-then-merge route (md:35) the landing merge commit does not exist at freeze time. As stated, this guard can only be a procedural pre-dispatch check or a comparison against an externally recorded value. The machine column of the split therefore overstates what can be enforced.
defects.evidence: md:59. json:2007 has requiredFrozenWorkflowSHA null. GitHub contexts doc: workflow_sha is 'The commit SHA for the workflow file.' Doc 77 CI-4 fix item 1 offered only an optional known-parent check, not a self-SHA guard.
defects.fix: Move the workflow SHA check to the procedural column: the dispatcher or the original reviewer verifies the landed commit and file hash before dispatch. Or replace it with doc 77's optional known-parent check, comparing the landed commit's first parent to the recorded pre-landing main tip at runtime.

defects.title: Missing statement that enforcement across refs and actors is procedural or repository-side
defects.claim: Once the workflow is on main, anyone with write access can dispatch with another ref, and that ref's own workflow bytes run, guards or not. In-file guards (event, ref, run_number, actor) bind only runs of the frozen main bytes. md:69 says a second fresh event's 'run_number guard must refuse pilot work', and md:61 classes the dispatcher check as a machine guard. Neither notes this limit. Doc 77's CI-4 fix ends: 'Enforcement across refs and actors beyond in-file guards stays procedural or repository-side.'
defects.evidence: md:59, md:61, md:69, md:71. json:2024-2029 lists the procedural restrictions but has no other-ref or modified-copy item. The GitHub manual-run doc says a branch can be selected with --ref and that 'Write access to the repository is required'. Doc 77 hl12 json:811-812 (CI-4 claim and fix).
defects.fix: Add one sentence in CI-4: in-file guards constrain only runs of the frozen main bytes; dispatches on other refs, modified copies and other actors are restricted procedurally or by repository settings. Add 'no dispatch on any other ref or of any modified workflow copy' to proceduralRestrictions.

itemChallenges.item: CI-4 one attempt and finite window
itemChallenges.note: Every element of smallestCorrection (4) is present: guards (md:59-60), concurrency (md:62), the named dispatcher (md:55, md:61), admission at runner start (md:64), the window choice (json:1995-1999), and a consumption rule covering pre-test refusals (md:69). md:67 also correctly says run_attempt alone cannot stop a second fresh dispatch. But this item's scope also requires an honest split between machine and procedural enforcement. That comes from the closing sentence of doc 77's CI-4 FIX (hl12 json:812): 'Enforcement across refs and actors beyond in-file guards stays procedural or repository-side.' Revision 2 omits that sentence, and its machine column overstates in three places. (a) md:59 lists 'exact frozen workflow SHA' as a guard in future frozen bytes. A file cannot contain the SHA of its own commit (M-2). Also, for workflow_dispatch, GITHUB_SHA is the 'Last commit on the GITHUB_REF branch', so the guard fails once main moves past the landing commit (MV-2). (b) md:69 says guards 'prevent the pilot setup/tests after guard refusal' and that the run_number guard 'must refuse' a second fresh event. That holds only for runs of the frozen main bytes, not for a modified copy dispatched on another ref (M-3). (c) The actor and notAfter values meant to be machine guards are bound only at step (6), after the freeze (M-4). md:71 states machine enforcement is NOT ESTABLISHED, and 'one authorized event' is procedural, so nothing unnamed is authorized. The defects are NONBLOCKING, but the split is incomplete, so the item is PARTIAL rather than CORRECTED.

missed.title: 'No inherited NODE_OPTIONS' conflicts with the inheritance the recommended heap option depends on
missed.claim: md:39 says 'no inherited NODE_OPTIONS or environment dump is permitted', and md:43 says to 'freeze both rather than assuming inherited settings'. The recommended NODE_OPTIONS option works only because Vitest's forked worker inherits NODE_OPTIONS from the orchestrator's process.env (doc 77, cli-api env spread).
